```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(dplyr)
library(tarr.pop)
```

This reference groups the public functions and supported methods by purpose. Each
category lists what its functions do and when they read or write population values.
Use `?function_name` for arguments and detailed contracts; for a dplyr method, use
help such as `?slice.poparray` or `?summarise.poparray`.

A `poparray` is an HDF5-backed, delayed array with named dimensions and metadata.
It requires distinct time and area roles. Coordinates such as year, county, age,
sex, and race/ethnicity are stored once on their axes rather than repeated in a
long table. Values occupy the combinations of those coordinates. Arrays have one
value type; data frames can have a different type in each column.

**Metadata only** operations inspect or update names, roles, and schemas without
reading population values. **Lazy view** operations record a subset, permutation,
or transformation. **Block computation** reads values now in bounded pieces;
`summarise()` and category collapsing belong here. **EAGER** conversions realize
the current cube view into memory. Filtering before computing or converting keeps
these boundaries manageable, but it does not replace overlap and applicability
checks.

## Storage locations and the cube registry

These functions configure storage or discover saved cubes. They manage files and
metadata rather than perform demographic aggregation.

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `cube_path()` | Read the active cube storage root. | Storage configuration. |
| `set_cube_path()` | Set and optionally persist the storage root. | Changes storage configuration. |
| `init_cubes()` | Prepare directories and initialize bundled cubes. | Creates storage and may copy files. |
| `rebuild_poparray_registry()` | Rebuild the catalog of saved cubes. | Scans cube metadata; updates registry. |
| `build_cube_if_missing()` | Invoke a supplied builder only when its cube is absent. | Builder determines computation and writes. |

Initialization is normally a setup step. Pass an explicit `filepath` to
`open_poparray()` when a script should use a known file independently of the local
series registry. The examples below use the bundled cube for that reason.

For call-sequence diagrams and a source-level explanation of the registry,
metadata cache, checkout, and constructor helpers, see
[How open_poparray() opens a population cube](open_poparray_internals.qmd).

## Opening, constructing, and saving cubes

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `open_poparray()` | Open a cube by file path or registered series ID. | Lazy `poparray`; reads metadata. |
| `open_tarr_pop()` | Compatibility entry point for opening a cube. | Delegates to `open_poparray()`. |
| `new_poparray()` | Wrap an HDF5-backed delayed array with explicit roles and semantics. | Constructs a `poparray` without extracting values. |
| `as.poparray()` | Convert supported inputs to a `poparray`. | Array input is written to HDF5; projection input produces a cube view. |
| `is.poparray()` | Test whether an object is a `poparray`. | Logical scalar. |
| `create_poparray()` | Write a `poparray` as a canonical saved cube. | Writes values and metadata to HDF5. |
| `save_poparray()` | Save the current cube view and metadata. | Computes the view while writing HDF5. |

Opening and saving have different costs: opening creates a delayed handle, while
saving writes the selected values. A temporary result from a reduction is not a
registered saved cube until explicitly persisted. Saving does not retain the
in-memory grouping setting.

```{r open_example}
example_path <- system.file("extdata", "tdc_example.h5", package = "tarr.pop")
example_pop <- open_poparray(filepath = example_path)
example_pop
```

## Importing and updating population records

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `ingest_population()` | Read and transform a source table, validate its dimensions and support, and persist a cube. | Reads a table; writes HDF5. |
| `add_population_data()` | Append new labels and their records on one dimension, such as a newly released year. | Validates records; writes a replacement cube. |

Both functions accept a reader and optional transformer. Define the dimensions,
semantics, completion policy, and provenance explicitly. Aggregate aliases such
as `"All"` are normally removed during ingestion. Missing combinations require a
completion policy; a structural exclusion is not automatically a zero population.
Updates record metadata revisions and coverage, but do not retain earlier
population arrays.

## Inspecting dimensions and coordinate labels

These accessors inspect coordinates and shape without reading population values.
Demographic helpers use semantic domains and conventional names; time and area
helpers follow roles even after renaming.

| Function / method | Purpose | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `dim()` | Read dimension extents. | Integer vector. |
| `names()` | Read dimension names. | Character vector. |
| `dimnames()` | Read all dimension coordinates. | Named list of label vectors. |
| `length()` | Read the total number of cells, not the number of axes. | Product of dimension extents. |
| `dim_labels()` | Read coordinates of any explicitly named dimension. | Character vector. |
| `times()`, `years()` | Read coordinates of the time role; `years()` aliases `times()`. | Character labels, including date labels. |
| `areas()` | Read coordinates of the area role. | Character labels. |
| `ages()` | Read the age-domain coordinates. | Interval-valued labels. |
| `sexes()` | Read sex-domain coordinates. | Character labels. |
| `races()` | Read a separate race-domain dimension when present. | Character labels. |
| `ethnicities()` | Read a separate ethnicity-domain dimension when present. | Character labels. |

Label accessors accept `remove` for literal or regex exclusions. A missing
required dimension raises an error; `missing = "null"` returns `NULL`. An empty
selection returns an empty label vector instead. The example stores combined
`race.eth` categories, so inspect that axis with `dim_labels()` rather than
assuming that separate race and ethnicity axes exist.

```{r inspect_labels}
names(example_pop)
dim(example_pop)
times(example_pop)
areas(example_pop)
head(ages(example_pop))
sexes(example_pop)
dim_labels(example_pop, "race.eth")
areas(example_pop, remove = stringr::regex("^D"))
```

## Reading and editing semantic and provenance metadata

| Function / replacement form | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `time_role()` | Read the time dimension name. | Metadata only. |
| `area_role()` | Read the area dimension name. | Metadata only. |
| `roles()`, `roles<-` | Read or replace time, area, and strata roles. | Validated role metadata. |
| `dim_semantics()`, `dim_semantics<-` | Read or replace per-dimension meaning, overlap declarations, and applicability schemas. | Semantic metadata. |
| `get_source()` | Read provenance from a cube object. | Metadata list. |
| `source_meta()`, `source_meta<-` | Read or replace provenance on an object or cube path. | Provenance metadata. |
| `data_col()`, `data_col<-` | Read or replace the population value-column name. | Character name used in summaries and tables. |
| `cube_metadata()`, `cube_metadata<-` | Read or replace roles, semantics, provenance, and value name as one bundle. | Validated metadata bundle. |

In-memory replacements edit the analysis object. Path-based replacements edit
the HDF5 metadata, record revisions, and require an elevated metadata role, for
example `options(tarr.pop.metadata_role = "admin")`. Reading metadata does not
require that role. Prefer a complete bundle when several dependent fields must
change together. Population values are not rewritten by metadata-only file edits.

```{r inspect_metadata}
time_role(example_pop)
area_role(example_pop)
roles(example_pop)
data_col(example_pop)
get_source(example_pop)
names(dim_semantics(example_pop))
```

## Filtering and selecting positions

| Function / method | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `[` | Subset by named or positional coordinates; `drop = FALSE` retains dimensions. | Lazy cube view. |
| `dplyr::filter()` | Select axis coordinates using label predicates. | Lazy cube view. |
| `%between%` | Express supported ordered-range predicates in `filter()`. | Predicate helper. |
| `age_overlaps()` | Find whole age categories overlapping requested age bounds. | Metadata-only logical index. |
| `dplyr::slice()` | Select integer positions on one explicit `.dimension`. | Lazy cube view. |
| `dplyr::slice_head()` | Select the first coordinates using `n` or `prop`. | Lazy cube view. |
| `dplyr::slice_tail()` | Select the last coordinates using `n` or `prop`. | Lazy cube view. |

`filter()` evaluates coordinate predicates rather than table-row predicates. Age
filters use interval meaning. Integer slice positions refer to the current view,
so position 1 after filtering may identify a different year from the original
cube. Slicing retains empty and singleton dimensions, trims applicability, rejects
duplicated retained positions, and preserves time order.

```{r select_coordinates}
tarrant <- example_pop |>
  dplyr::filter(area.name == "Tarrant", year %between% c(2016, 2018))
areas(tarrant)
times(tarrant)

first_two_years <- example_pop |>
  dplyr::slice(1:2, .dimension = "year")
latest_two_years <- example_pop |>
  dplyr::slice_tail(n = 2, .dimension = "year")
first_half <- example_pop |>
  dplyr::slice_head(prop = 0.5, .dimension = "year")
times(first_two_years)
times(latest_two_years)
times(first_half)
```

The edge helpers default to one coordinate, truncate oversized requests, and use
dplyr's rounding rules for `prop`. Negative sizes retain the dimension size minus
the requested number or proportion. With `slice()`, zeros and out-of-range
positions are ignored; missing or fractional positions are errors. Slice helpers
require `.dimension` and do not support `by` or other grouped-slicing arguments.
Dropping required role dimensions through `[` can return a general delayed array
instead of a `poparray`.

## Renaming and reordering dimensions

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `dplyr::rename()` | Rename dimensions with `new_name = old_name`. | Lazy metadata update. |
| `dplyr::rename_with()` | Transform selected dimension names with a function. | Lazy metadata update. |
| `dplyr::relocate()` | Move dimensions with tidy-select and `.before` or `.after`. | Delayed axis permutation. |

These verbs preserve coordinate labels and population values. Role names,
semantic names, applicability controller references, and grouping follow each
renamed axis. `relocate()` changes axis order, not label order or HDF5 chunking.
Benchmark an actual workflow before claiming that a particular axis order speeds
up disk access.

```{r rename_and_relocate}
renamed <- latest_two_years |>
  dplyr::rename(time = year, county = area.name)
names(renamed)
time_role(renamed)

snake_names <- latest_two_years |>
  dplyr::rename_with(~ gsub(".", "_", .x, fixed = TRUE), dplyr::contains("."))
names(snake_names)

age_first <- first_two_years |>
  dplyr::relocate(age.char, .before = year)
names(age_first)
```

`rename_with()` must return one character name per selected axis, including
`character(0)` for an empty selection. Missing, blank, or duplicated resulting
names are rejected. Computed values and row-oriented sorting are not part of
these dimension operations.

## Checking overlaps and combining categories

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `overlaps()` | Inspect active overlap risks and declared overlapping levels. | Metadata inspection. |
| `drop_overlap_levels()` | Remove declared overlap-causing labels from a view. | Lazy subsetting; does not resolve every possible interval overlap. |
| `collapse_dim()` | Combine selected labels within one axis by guarded population sums. | Block computation; temporary HDF5 result. |
| `collapse_all()` | Collapse every label on selected axes into one level each. | Sequential guarded block computations. |
| `group_ages()` | Build age bands using interval-aware contributor grouping. | Guarded category reduction. |

Category grouping creates new categories; analysis grouping in the next section
retains existing coordinate combinations. Both must respect semantic safety.
Overlapping age intervals and race categories can double-count people. Filter to
non-overlapping contributors or define valid age bands before summing. The
example contains open-ended age categories alongside single older ages, so the
summary example below selects the disjoint single ages 1–84. Infant and older-age
counts are deliberately outside that example’s scope.

With applicability schemas, category reducers exclude structurally unavailable
contributors before summation. They preserve applicable missing values and warn
when requested groups cannot be derived. `drop = TRUE` removes a collapsed
singleton axis only when it is not a required role or applicability controller.

## Grouping axes and summarising population values

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `dplyr::group_by()` | Record axes whose coordinate combinations stay distinct in a summary. | Metadata only; same cube values. |
| `dplyr::ungroup()` | Remove all or selected grouping axes from the analysis setting. | Metadata only; no axes removed. |
| `dplyr::group_vars()` | Inspect grouping dimension names in order. | Character vector. |
| `dplyr::groups()` | Inspect grouping dimensions as symbols. | Symbol list. |
| `dplyr::summarise()`, `dplyr::summarize()` | Sum one population measure over ungrouped axes. | Guarded block computation; HDF5-backed cube. |

`group_by()` declares which dimensions stay distinct in a summary. It records
metadata without reading population values. `ungroup()` removes all grouping,
or only selected grouping dimensions; it does not remove axes or alter values.
Use `group_vars()` or `groups()` to inspect the setting. Grouping follows named
subsetting, filtering, slicing, renaming, and relocation. It is an analysis setting
in memory: saving and reopening an HDF5 cube returns an ungrouped object.

`summarise()` (also spelled `summarize()`) currently accepts one named population
sum, such as `total = sum(population)`. The input value name must match
`data_col(pop)`. Grouping axes remain in their original dimension order, and all
other dimensions are summed and removed. Both required roles, time and area, and
all applicability-controller dimensions must be grouped. This prevents a summary
from losing the information required to interpret a `poparray`.

```{r group_and_summarise}
# Select explicit, disjoint single ages 1–84. This is a subtotal for that
# age range, retaining sex and race/ethnicity as separate groups.
single_ages <- example_pop[age.char = as.character(1:84), drop = FALSE]
grouped <- single_ages |>
  dplyr::group_by(year, area.name, sex, race.eth)
dplyr::group_vars(grouped)

totals <- grouped |>
  dplyr::summarise(total = sum(population), .groups = "drop")
names(dimnames(totals))
data_col(totals)
dplyr::group_vars(totals)

# Temporary grouping gives the same values and leaves the result ungrouped.
totals_by <- single_ages |>
  dplyr::summarise(total = sum(population),
                   .by = c(year, area.name, sex, race.eth))

# Removing grouping never reduces the underlying cube.
dplyr::group_vars(dplyr::ungroup(grouped, sex))
```

Summary grouping defaults to `"drop_last"`; use `.groups = "keep"` to retain
every grouping dimension, or `"drop"` to remove grouping metadata. These options
leave the retained cube dimensions intact. `.by` selects grouping for one
operation and always returns an ungrouped result; it cannot be combined with
existing grouping or `.groups`. `.add = TRUE` in `group_by()` appends grouping
dimensions. Computed groups, `.drop = FALSE`, rowwise summaries, arbitrary summary
expressions, and multiple summary measures are not supported by this first version.

Summarising is a computation boundary: it reads bounded source blocks and writes
temporary HDF5 results. It avoids loading the full cube and returns a result on
which later operations remain delayed. Overlap checks for every reduced axis run
before the first population read. Double storage prevents integer overflow in
summed counts. When every axis is retained and `na.rm = FALSE`, or there are no
output coordinate combinations, only metadata and delayed views are changed.

Applicable missing counts propagate by default; `sum(population, na.rm = TRUE)`
omits them. Structural exclusions follow applicability metadata, and outputs with
no applicable contributors remain `NA` with a reducer warning. Retained categories
that are structurally inapplicable are masked to `NA`. Empty retained dimensions
produce empty cubes; empty reduced dimensions raise an informative error.
The source note records the summary and its retained and reduced axes.

For a small ordinary base R array, `apply()` can produce a reference sum, but it
does not enforce cube semantics. Converting a full `poparray` to a base array or
tibble for that purpose is **EAGER**; use the guarded cube summary instead.


## Applying functions to coordinate slices

| Function / method | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `split()` | Create one named delayed slice per label of a dimension. | List of lazy views. |
| `by()` | Apply `FUN` to those slices, optionally simplifying results. | `FUN` determines reads and computation. |

Use these when a per-coordinate operation is needed outside the supported summary
expression. They do not record the grouping metadata used by `summarise()`.
Retain `drop = FALSE` when each slice must remain a `poparray`.

## Computing whole-view statistics

| Function / method | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `sum()` | Compute a semantically guarded total over the current view. | Reads values; scalar result. |
| `min()`, `max()` | Compute the smallest and largest values. | Backend scan; scalar results. |
| `range()` | Compute both extrema. | Backend scan; two-element result. |
| `mean()` | Compute the mean value. | Backend reduction; scalar result. |
| `var()`, `sd()` | Compute variance and standard deviation. | Backend reductions; scalar results. |
| `summary()` | Compute descriptive statistics and missingness for the current view. | Reads values; summary vector. |

These operations compute now even when the input is delayed. Filter the cube to
the intended population and period first. `summarise()` retains named group axes;
a whole-view `sum()` returns a scalar instead. Do not add repeated snapshots
across years as though they were distinct people in one population.

```{r one_group_total}
one_group <- totals |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2018, area.name == "Tarrant",
                sex == "female", race.eth == "white")
sum(one_group)
```

## Converting arrays and tables

| Function / method | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `as.array()` | Retrieve the current view as an ordinary array. | **EAGER**. |
| `as.data.frame()` | Expand cube coordinates and values into a long data frame. | **EAGER**. |
| `tibble::as_tibble()` | Expand a cube into a long tibble. | **EAGER**. |
| `as.double()` | Coerce the delayed cube backend to double while preserving metadata and grouping. | Delayed type conversion. |
| `array_2_df()` | Convert an ordinary array into a long data frame. | In-memory representation conversion. |
| `df_2_array()` | Convert a source data frame into an ordinary array. | In-memory array construction. |

Conversion costs scale with the selected cells. Keep the cube form through
filtering and reductions, then convert only the result needed for reporting,
plotting, or downstream tools. Base arrays and tables do not automatically enforce
`poparray` overlap or applicability contracts.

```{r small_table}
# This result contains one year, county, sex, and race/ethnicity combination.
# The conversion is EAGER, but the selected result is small.
tibble::as_tibble(one_group)
```

## Forecasting and inspecting projections

| Function / method | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `project()` | Fit forecasts from an observed population cube. | Computes forecasts; returns `poparray_projection`. |
| `poparray_projection()` | Construct a projection object with values, uncertainty, and forecast metadata. | Projection constructor. |
| `projection()` | Extract the projected values from a projection object. | `poparray` view. |
| `std_error()` | Extract the associated standard errors. | `poparray` view. |
| `confint()` | Obtain projection confidence bounds for a requested level. | Projection result. |
| `as.poparray()` on a projection | Obtain its population-cube representation. | HDF5-backed cube view. |
| `as.data.frame()` or `tibble::as_tibble()` on a projection | Retrieve a long projection table. | **EAGER**. |
| `plot()` on a projection | Display projected trajectories or population pyramids. | Reads values to create a plot. |
| `print()` on a projection | Display forecast metadata and dimensions. | Object inspection. |

Observed cubes and projection cubes have different contracts. The new grouping
and summary methods in this reference operate on `poparray`; convert a projection
explicitly when a base-cube analysis is appropriate. Select the needed dimensions
before tabular retrieval. Consult `?project` for model choices and forecast-level
arguments.

## Inspecting metadata history and repairing metadata

| Function | Purpose | Execution / result |
|---|---|---|
| `cube_version()` | Inspect schema version, cube ID, and current metadata revision. | Metadata only. |
| `cube_history()` | Read the committed metadata revision catalog. | Metadata tibble. |
| `cube_metadata_at()` | Inspect a historical revision's metadata and coordinate coverage. | Historical metadata snapshot. |
| `update_cube_metadata()` | Validate and write a complete metadata bundle with a recorded reason. | Metadata write; elevated role required. |
| `restore_cube_metadata()` | Restore a compatible snapshot as a new revision. | Metadata write; current coverage must match. |
| `recover_cube_metadata()` | Repair staging groups after an interrupted metadata replacement. | Metadata recovery; elevated role required. |

History records semantics, coverage, and provenance, not copies of previous
population arrays. Restoring metadata does not restore old population values or
reverse a schema migration. File-based edits are single-writer operations. Use
in-memory replacements for an analysis view and path-based administration when
intentionally changing stored cube metadata.

## Choosing a workflow

Open a cube, inspect its named roles and coordinates, then filter and reshape its
lazy view. Check overlap and applicability before category reductions or grouped
sums. Compute the required result and convert only the selected output to a table.

The dplyr verbs cataloged above have cube-specific methods. Importing dplyr does
not provide `poparray` implementations of `select()`, `mutate()`, joins,
`arrange()`, or rowwise operations. A conversion to a tibble enables ordinary table
verbs, with the explicit **EAGER** cost and responsibility to preserve demographic
meaning.
